match.reason: The closest bank point, eng-context-values-paired-texts, is about using the contexts of two texts to explain how a shared story is treated differently, which is broader and more comparative than the new point's focus on identifying values a single text shows, so no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Values in a text
card: A value is something a person or group believes is important, such as loyalty, justice, honesty or freedom.
the values a character holds, shown through what they say, choose and do. A character who gives up a reward to protect a friend shows loyalty.
the values the text seems to support or question. A writer can show a character's value as admirable, or can make readers doubt it.
To find a value, ask what the characters care about and what the text invites readers to think of it. A character's values and the text's values can differ.
draft.remember: A value is what matters to someone. Ask who holds it and how the text treats it.

a.q: In a story, Priya lies to her teacher to cover for her friend, and the narrator shows her as brave. Which value does Priya's choice show?
a.why: Priya puts her friend's interests first, even at a cost to herself, which is loyalty. Honesty is the tempting option, but she lies, so her choice does not show honesty.

b.q: In a novel, a mine owner in a small town refuses to pay fair wages. The narrator describes him in cold, mocking language, and the workers are shown with warmth. What does the text seem to do with the owner's values?
opts: Question them, by presenting his greed as unjust
Support them, because he holds power in the town
Ignore them, because he is not the main character
Support them, because the narrator describes him closely
b.why: The cold, mocking language towards the owner and the warmth towards the workers invite readers to see his behaviour as unjust, so the text questions his values. A character holding power does not mean the text approves of how he uses it.
b.clue: Notice how the narrator treats the owner compared with the workers.

b.best: Question them, by presenting his greed as unjust
